note:
NATURAL, not seeded. Copied verbatim from `docs/backlog/wi-034-execution-policy-migration.md`, a work-item record written for its own purpose months before this harness existed. No marker was planted, and the key is derived from what the passage holds rather than from what an author decided to put there.

This case was REJECTED once and rebuilt. The first version was authored by an agent that copied this same source and then inserted `In summary,` and `crucial` into it -- its own rationale said the two hits `were placed mechanically`. That is a seeded case wearing a natural label, which is the exact author bias guide section 6.5 exists to remove, and the adversarial lens assigned to catch it did not. Verified by diffing the fixture against the source file.

What it measures: the lexicon finds exactly TWO markers here and BOTH are things the skill's own rules say are not findings -- `align` as a genuine technical verb (`config keys were aligned`), and a SINGLE em dash, where pattern 9 states in its own words that one em dash is punctuation and is not reported. A correct run therefore changes very little. This is the false-positive question of E2 asked against prose nobody wrote for the test.
must_keep: config keys were made to match
must_not_appear_notes: Reinjection guards. The failure this case is built to catch is the skill's own named one -- over-editing INTRODUCES the patterns the pass exists to remove. None of these surfaces is in the fixture, so `must_drop` cannot express the check: TC-EV-27 refuses a removal check for something never present, and rightly. `crucial` and `In summary` are on this list because the rejected first version of this case had an agent insert exactly those two words into this exact passage.
min_similarity_derivation: DECLARED, not fitted, and set to the same 0.75 the E3 control uses, for the same reason: a text carrying nothing the skill should act on must come back close to unchanged. It is not moved to make a run green.
what_a_failing_run_looks_like: A run that 'fixes' `aligned` because the word is on the [A] list, or that removes the single em dash, or that re-voices technically exact prose into something smoother and loses `analyze_gaps.py` or the 31/2 figures. Any of those drops similarity below 0.75 or loses an anchor.
natural_source_notes: Guide section 6.5: a set where the author planted every defect measures the author. This fixture is copied VERBATIM from the file above, which was written for its own purpose. TC-EV-72 re-reads that file and fails if the fixture is not a substring of it -- the check that caught an agent inserting two markers into this exact kind of passage and calling the result natural. The fixture is an EXCERPT: two paragraphs of that file with a results table between them elided. Each paragraph is verbatim; the guard checks them one by one rather than checking the join, which no source file contains.
must_keep_notes: Several anchors are LISTS of surface forms. Each list states the same fact in spellings a faithful rewrite may legitimately choose -- a numeral for a word, a contraction for its expansion, a different verb for the same event. The alternatives say what the fact IS; none of them would be satisfied by a run that dropped or changed it. The CANONICAL form is first and is the one the fixture holds, which is what TC-EV-26 checks. An anchor whose identity is the claim itself -- a name, a code, an exact figure -- deliberately carries no alternative.
